rows.label: Take the introductory linguistics course, LING 1101
rows.note: Must be taken at Cornell, so exam and transfer credit does not count.

rows.label: Take one foundation course: phonetics and phonology, syntax and semantics, or historical linguistics
rows.note: Must be taken at Cornell, so exam and transfer credit does not count.

rows.label: Take three more linguistics courses of 3+ credits, at most one at the 1000 level and at least one at 3000 or above
rows.note: Counts LING courses and cross-listings of 3 or more credits taken at Cornell. First-year writing seminars (by title) and variable-credit courses (which can be taken under 3 credits) are held out; language-instruction courses the catalog identifies (Old Norse I and II, Cayuga Language and Culture I and II, Old Irish I and II) are held out by title, and a confirm row covers language courses under other cross-listed codes. The credit target of 10 follows from the 18-credit minimum.

limits.label: At most one of these at the 1000 level
At least one of these at the 3000 level or above

rows.label: Do not count first-year writing seminars or language courses as linguistics courses
rows.note: The board holds out writing seminars by title only; check any language-instruction course yourself.

rows.label: Count only courses taken for 3 or more credits among the three additional courses
rows.note: The board leaves out variable-credit courses (such as independent study); if you took one for 3 or more credits, count it by hand.

rows.label: Courses approved for the linguistics major count toward the five courses; confirm any such course with the department
rows.note: The board counts only LING courses and cross-listings; an approved course from another department is yours to add by hand.

rows.label: Any substitution for these requirements needs a petition to your advisor and approval by the director of undergraduate studies
Take every qualifying course at Cornell for a letter grade (no S/U or SX/UX)
rows.note: The board already leaves out exam and transfer credit; the letter-grade rule is yours to check.

rows.label: Finish each counting course with a grade of C- or better
Earn a B- or better in LING 1101 and in at least one other LING course that counts toward the minor
Meet with the linguistics DUS or your assigned minor advisor to plan courses when you declare
